item.title: Indonesia Rain Set to Ease Toxic Haze in Singapore, Malaysia
item.description: Indonesia is set for more consistent rain next month, providing relief from wildfires that have spewed toxic smoke across Singapore and Malaysia, though widespread downpours are still weeks away.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- Indonesia is set for more consistent rain next month, providing relief from wildfires that have spewed toxic smoke across Singapore and Malaysia, though widespread downpours are still weeks away.Rainfall has picked up across Indonesia in recent days, helping to replenish soil moisture after months of severe drought triggered by El Niño, according to weather data. While that’s offered some respite, heavier rain isn’t expected until at least early December in regions such as Kalimantan, where blazes have raged and most of the remaining fire hotspots are located.The choking haze from Indonesia’s worst fire season in years has cloaked local towns and drifted across neighboring countries for weeks, closing schools, driving demand for air purifiers and straining diplomatic ties. Singapore’s foreign minister visited Jakarta this week to ease widening tensions, with the two countries agreeing to establish a joint taskforce on forest fires.Indonesia has received less than a quarter of its normal rainfall since June, according to Atmospheric G2, leaving the landscape bone-dry and making fires often linked to slash-and-burn agricultural practices harder to contain. Nearly 13,500 hotspots have been detected nationwide so far this month, the most since 2015, and adding to high counts in September and August, the forestry ministry’s SiPongi platform shows.“Substantial rainfall should fall through November, generally increasing further in December and remaining significant into early 2027,” said Andreas Vallgren, chief science officer at weather intelligence firm Ignitia. “Whether this is sufficient to extinguish existing fires, particularly in peatlands, will depend on how consistently rainfall reaches the affected areas.”Over recent weeks, Kuala Lumpur and Singapore have frequently topped the rankings of the world’s most polluted cities, according to data from IQAir. The city-state has flagged possible legal action against companies suspected of illegal burning, while more than 1,000 people protested in central Jakarta on Wednesday over the government’s handling of the fires.Indonesia’s agricultural activity has been impacted. Smog from the wildfires is impairing the activity of weevils that pollinate oil palms in the world’s biggest grower, while haze is slowing harvesting at estates owned by major producer SD Guthrie Bhd. in Kalimantan and Sumatra, and could weigh on productivity.The combination of fires and dry weather has prompted the Indonesian Palm Oil Association to trim its production estimates for next year to 56.6 million tons, a two-year low, according to M. Hadi Sugeng Wahyudiono, secretary-general of the industry group. That compares with an earlier forecast of 59 million tons. Still, forecasts point to improving conditions. Near-normal rainfall is expected next month, helping to prevent new fires from developing and curb the spread of existing blazes, according to weather forecasting startup Plannette AI. “Rains will ease fires in Borneo and Sumatra” by December, said Chief Executive Officer and founder Hansi Singh.Indonesian authorities are hopeful the fire crisis can be resolved in November, said Budi Harsoyo, a senior official at the country’s national weather agency, known as BMKG. Satellite monitoring suggests that the development of hotspots in three provinces hit hardest by fires may be letting up, he added.There are rising chances of monthly rainfall exceeding 300 millimeters (11.8 inches) in parts of South Sumatra, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan in December, BMKG said this week. Precipitation is expected to pick up in the first week of the month, according to an outlook from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts.One wildcard risk, said Ignitia’s Vallgren, is that the persistence of fires and smoke can crimp rainfall, because the smog blocks sunrays and inhibits the convective process that forms storms and showers. History offers a cautionary tale. In 1997, blazes that burned and grew during the prolonged dry season that year were briefly suppressed when rains finally arrived in December, weeks later than normal, but reignited in early 1998 as the rainy season ended prematurely due to a lingering El Niño.“There is a feedback loop — more fires mean more smoke, which can act to suppress rainfall, which in turn can delay rainfall,” Vallgren said. On the other hand, “if some strong rainfall events make it, they do help to clean the air to some degree, which helps kick-start more frequent storms.”More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Iran Receives Vance Letter, Signals No Shift in Peace Deal Terms
item.description: Iran received a letter sent by US Vice President JD Vance to its top security official, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported, with one of the country’s top negotiators later suggesting Tehran’s positions on ending the war will not be compromised.
item.dc:creator: list.metadata.agency
item.content:encoded: (Bloomberg) -- Iran received a letter sent by US Vice President JD Vance to its top security official, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported, with one of the country’s top negotiators later suggesting Tehran’s positions on ending the war will not be compromised. Tasnim didn’t disclose the contents of the letter addressed to Mohsen Rezaee, the hardline chief of the Supreme National Security Council, or say whether Tehran is preparing a reply. But in a post on X after the letter was reportedly received, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, one of Iran’s negotiators in previous talks to end the war, wrote that “Iran’s conditions have been repeatedly and clearly stated to the mediators.” “The carrot-and-stick approach has no effect on Iran,” Ghalibaf continued without mentioning Vance’s letter or saying if his comments constituted a formal reply. The highly unusual approach by Vance comes as President Donald Trump repeatedly threatens to resume airstrikes on Iran amid an impasse in negotiations to end the eight-month war. Trump told reporters on Wednesday he authorized Vance to contact Tehran, saying the letter was meant to assist Iran with “medical supplies and various things,” without providing specifics.The Wall Street Journal earlier reported that Vance had written to Rezaee in a bid to revive peace negotiations. The development follows high-level talks in Tehran this week with officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan. The parties described the meeting as positive and agreed to continue discussions, though no formal second round has been set. Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei reiterated earlier this week that his country has certain conditions that must be met before an end to the war can be agreed. At the heart of the impasse is Tehran’s ongoing attacks on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, while the US has imposed a naval blockade on Iran’s ports. Iran has repeatedly said in recent weeks that it remains open to diplomacy, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi writing on X on Thursday that while “our Brave Armed Forces are fully prepared to defend the Homeland, Iran continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed.”The US and Israel started bombing Iran in late February, triggering retaliatory strikes by Tehran on Gulf nations hosting US military bases. The war has killed thousands — mostly Iranian civilians — while disrupting energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and roiling global markets.--With assistance from Eltaf Najafizada and Sherif Tarek.More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Why are Wall Street firms paying up to $100k a month for faster access to Trump's Truth Social posts? Any specific goal?
item.description: Bloomberg and two trading firms have reportedly agreed to pay Donald Trump’s Truth Social for faster access to his posts, as per Reuters. The company is already facing a lawsuit or faster access to government information. Here's why it is happening.
item.dc:creator: Sneha Biswas
item.content:encoded: Wall Street trading firms and financial data providers are paying as much as $100,000 a month for faster access to US President Donald Trump’s posts on Truth Social. The move is reportedly aimed at seeking an edge in financial markets where Trump's statements can trigger movements.Truth Social, the social media platform founded by Trump, has signed up Bloomberg, Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading for its Truth API service, Reuters reported, citing sources.What is Truth Social's API serviceThe API enables subscribers to receive Trump’s posts faster than any human could by manually checking the platform.The service is said to give subscribers a timing advantage. It is reported to be ahead around 50 milliseconds, according to Trump Media officials. That difference might seem insignificant but can matter to high-frequency trading firms, especially those who rely on algorithmic and automated strategies to respond to market movement.Why trading firms are ready to pay for itThese firms use software that ingests news headlines, company announcements and government statements, analyses the information and can execute trades, all within thousandths of a second, as per the news agency. Faster access to Trump’s posts can potentially help them react before others in the market, including investors.Trump’s social media statements have moved markets from time to time. Oil futures sank after he announced a ceasefire in the Iran war via Truth Social in April.Trump Media and Technology Group announced the fastest-access product in July. In August, the company told investors it had “signed more than 10 customer agreements”, which neither Reuters nor Live Mint could confirm.Trump Media said the customers were primarily trade firms from Wall Street who reportedly paid between $60,000 and $100,000 every month. Why service is controversial for TrumpWhat makes this deal even more significant is that it marks the first time a business tied to a sitting president has sold access to his statements. It also prompted ethical and legal concerns among a section of people on the internet.Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren and Adam Schiff asked the US Securities and Exchange Commission in July to investigate whether the service violated securities laws and called it a “shocking abuse” of office by a president for personal gain.Trump Media said, as per Reuters, “Truth Social offers an industry-standard API product for which there is significant demand across industries. We take customer confidentiality seriously. This reporting is based on misleading information being peddled by anonymous sources aimed at harming our company, customers and shareholders.”The company is also facing a lawsuit by Intercept Media and the Freedom of the Press Foundation. It alleges that charging for faster access to government information would violate the First Amendment and Fifth Amendment rights of the public.
